title: Container With Most Water
description: Given an array of n line heights, pick two lines that together with the x-axis form a container holding the most water (width times the shorter height). Return that maximum area.

reference.use_case: Choosing two boundary points that maximize capacity when capacity is capped by the weaker boundary and grows with the distance between them, such as placing two walls along a terrain profile to hold the most water.
system_examples: GIS/terrain analysis — evaluating retaining-wall or levee placements along an elevation profile
Capacity planning over a timeline — finding the widest span whose two bounding checkpoints both sustain a minimum level
reference.explanation: Start with the widest pair; the shorter side can never be part of a better answer at a narrower width, so discard it and move inward, giving O(n) instead of O(n²). Direct industry uses are limited; the lasting value is the proof technique for safely pruning a two-sided search space.
